description: Explicit decisions for specialized theme near-color pairs. Keep this file in sync with scripts/audit-theme-colors.mjs output; lower the audit baseline when a pair is merged.

decisions.reason: Tokyo Night structural chrome uses the canonical Tokyo base hue around storm-indigo content; #1c1c1f is the default dark/china/slate neutral surface. Merging would flatten cross-theme identity rather than remove an app-level duplicate.
decisions.reevaluateWhen: Only after a visual review proves Tokyo Night no longer needs a distinct structural chrome identity.

decisions.reason: Midnight content, raised panels, and editor lineHighlight are adjacent in the same dark theme. Merging would weaken surface and editor-row separation.
decisions.reevaluateWhen: Only after a Midnight surface-ramp redesign removes the adjacent role split.

decisions.reason: The first value is the light xterm blue and the second is the light workbench link hover. They belong to different renderer and document interaction semantics.
decisions.reevaluateWhen: Reevaluate only when terminal ANSI and workbench link roles share a reviewed palette contract.

decisions.reason: Claude Night keeps the reference warm near-black #141413 as its canvas, while #0e0e10 is the canonical recessed neutral the other dark builtins already declare. Merging would either flatten the Claude warm-black identity or restyle unrelated dark appearances.
decisions.reevaluateWhen: Only after a reviewed warm-neutral recessed ramp is shared by every dark builtin palette.

decisions.reason: Claude elevated surfaces are deliberately warm (#262421) to preserve the reference brown-black cast, while #262626 is the canonical neutral raised stop of the existing dark builtins. Color temperature is the identity being preserved here.
decisions.reevaluateWhen: Only after the dark builtin palettes agree on a single raised-surface temperature.

decisions.reason: Claude uses ivory #f0eee6 as a chrome band that must read as a lighter layer above the recessed content inset #f5f3e8. They are two role-separated steps of one warm surface ramp inside a single theme.
decisions.reevaluateWhen: Only after a Claude surface review unifies the chrome band and content inset roles.

decisions.reason: Cross-theme identity: #f0ede0 is the China Style rice-paper surface and #f0eee6 is the Claude chrome ivory band. Neither appearance can adopt the other value without losing the palette it was sampled from.
decisions.reevaluateWhen: Only after China Style and Claude share one reviewed paper and ivory token.

decisions.reason: The Claude reference forbids pure white, so its canvas stays at #fcfcfb, while the default Light appearance intentionally keeps pure white surfaces. The gap encodes two different product appearances rather than a duplicated role.
decisions.reevaluateWhen: Only after every light appearance adopts one reviewed canvas off-white value.
